elements.quote: We extracted data on the following items: sample size; study design; year(s) of data collection; country/region; data source; procedure or treatment (disease); definition of minimum volume standard; outcomes; (unadjusted and adjusted) effect measures with corresponding confidence intervals and/or p values; statistical models; and adjusting variables.
elements.reason: The manuscript lists several data items collected; however, it does not provide definitions for all variables listed, as required by PRISMA 10b.
No description of assumptions made about missing or unclear study information is reported in the retrieved methods or elsewhere.
While a standardized data extraction tool was developed in Excel, no cited tool or framework used to determine which data items to collect is reported.

elements.quote: Risk of bias was assessed using the 'Risk Of Bias In Non- Randomised Studies-of Interventions' (ROBINS- I) tool.
elements.reason: The tool used (ROBINS-I) is named, but no version information is provided.

elements.quote: Across all outcomes examined in the studies, the risk of bias pertaining to the selection of both exposed and non- exposed populations, as well as classification of intervention, deviation from intended intervention, missing data and measurement of outcomes was determined to be low. For two studies, the possibility of bias due to selection of reported results was considered to be low.
elements.reason: The domains/components assessed correspond to ROBINS-I domains and are explicitly listed.

elements.quote: The risk of bias was moderate for results on outcomes for two studies and serious for seven studies (see online supplemental material 6).
elements.reason: An overall risk-of-bias judgement is reported, but the rules used to derive overall judgements from domain-level assessments are not described.

elements.quote: For quality assessment, the ROBINS- I tool, with additions for CBA and ITS study designs, 28 was independently applied by two reviewers (AP, JS).
elements.reason: The manuscript acknowledges adaptations (“additions for CBA and ITS”) but does not describe what the adaptations entailed.
No newly developed risk-of-bias tool was used; an existing tool (ROBINS-I) was applied.

elements.quote: For quality assessment, the ROBINS- I tool, with additions for CBA and ITS study designs, 28 was independently applied by two reviewers (AP, JS). For both data collection and quality assessment, any disagreement was resolved by discussion and consensus.
elements.reason: Reports two reviewers, that they worked independently, and how disagreements were resolved.
No processes are reported for obtaining or confirming risk-of-bias information from study investigators.
No automation tools for risk-of-bias assessment are reported.

elements.quote: For dichotomous outcomes, we used the risk ratio (RR) ... or the ratio of RRs (ie, the RR postintervention/RR preintervention), if possible. For continuous outcomes, we used the absolute change ... Alternatively, we used the relative change ... For ITS studies, if possible, we relied on the results either obtained by a regression including time trends before and after the intervention ... We used segmented regression models ... to estimate level change and slope parameters associated with the intervention.
elements.reason: They explicitly specify the effect measures by outcome type: RRs (or ratio of RRs) for dichotomous outcomes, absolute or relative change for continuous outcomes, and level and slope changes from segmented regression/ITS for time series.
No thresholds or ranges (e.g., for interpreting magnitude of effects) are used or discussed; the synthesis reports conventional estimates with confidence intervals only.
The review does not describe re-expressing results into different effect measures; it specifies primary measures (RRs, absolute/relative changes, ITS level/slope) without conversion methods.

elements.quote: For data synthesis and statistical analyses, we followed the guidance published by the Cochrane EPOC group.
elements.reason: They provide a general justification by citing adherence to Cochrane EPOC guidance, but do not give specific rationales for choosing particular effect measures for individual outcomes.

The retrieved text describes overall inclusion criteria, screening, and statistical methods (e.g., study designs included, re-analysis approach, outcome selection), but does not explicitly describe the processes used to decide which studies were eligible for each specific synthesis or how studies were grouped/mapped to syntheses.

elements.quote: For dichotomous outcomes, we used the risk ratio (RR) obtained from statistical analyses adjusting for baseline differences ... or the ratio of RRs (ie, the RR postintervention/RR preintervention), if possible. For continuous outcomes, we used the absolute change obtained from a statistical analysis that was adjusted for baseline differences ... Alternatively, we used the relative change adjusted for baseline differences in the outcome measures. ... If papers with a before- after design did not provide an appropriate analysis or reporting of results to be included in this systematic review, but presented the needed data points in a readable graph or in a table, we re- analysed the data ourselves. We used segmented regression models, specifically ARIMA models with two external variables, to estimate level change and slope parameters associated with the intervention. ... We used the ' auto. arima' function from the R- package 'forecast' to select the most appropriate ARIMA model based on Akaike Information Criterion (AIC) and Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC).
elements.reason: The authors describe data preparation and conversion methods used for synthesis, including deriving effect measures (ratio of RRs, absolute and relative changes adjusted for baseline), and reanalyzing studies by extracting data from tables/graphs and fitting segmented regression/ARIMA models with model selection criteria. These are explicit methods to prepare data for presentation and synthesis.

elements.quote: In total, we located 12 878 records through electronic databases and trial registries, while an additional 642 records were discovered through reference lists of included articles, forward citation searches, and by contacting authors directly.
elements.reason: Reports the numbers of records identified from databases/registries and other sources, but does not report numbers removed before screening, the number screened, or excluded after initial screening.

elements.quote: After examining 241 full- text reports, 9 studies 35-43 were subsequently included (see PRISMA flow diagram in online supplemental material 4).
elements.reason: Provides the number of reports assessed for eligibility (241), but does not report numbers of reports sought, not retrieved, or the numbers excluded with primary reasons.

elements.quote: After examining 241 full- text reports, 9 studies 35-43 were subsequently included
elements.reason: Reports the number of included studies (9), but does not report the number of included reports.
No information about ongoing studies or associated reports is provided in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: Design Systematic review using the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach.
elements.reason: The manuscript presents a standalone systematic review with protocol registration; there is no indication that this is an update of a previous review, so reporting prior review totals does not apply.

elements.quote: Two reviewers (JS, SP- H) independently screened titles and abstracts of all identified articles.
elements.reason: Screening was conducted by human reviewers; no automation tools for record exclusion are reported, so distinguishing human vs automation exclusions does not apply.

The retrieved evidence does not provide a list of excluded studies that appeared eligible with specific reasons for exclusion. A PRISMA flow diagram is referenced as supplemental material, but no citations of excluded studies or their reasons are reported in the provided text.

elements.quote: After examining 241 full- text reports, 9 studies 35-43 were subsequently included (see PRISMA flow diagram in online supplemental material 4).
elements.reason: The results section explicitly cites all included studies as references 35–43, indicating each included study is cited.

elements.quote: All study characteristics including study designs, countries, patient characteristics and diseases are presented in online supplemental material 1.
elements.reason: Authors state that key study characteristics for all included studies are presented in a supplemental table, supporting comparison.

elements.quote: We chose the following five outcomes, measured and reported in six studies, 35-37 40-42 as outcomes of importance for assessing the effect of minimum volume standards interventions in hospitals: ... Table 1 presents the characteristics of interventions and findings for all outcomes of importance.
elements.reason: Intervention details are tabulated (Table 1) but only for six studies with outcomes of importance, not for every included study.

elements.quote: The risk of bias was moderate for results on outcomes for two studies and serious for seven studies (see online supplemental material 6). Across all outcomes examined in the studies, the risk of bias pertaining to the selection of both exposed and non- exposed populations, as well as classification of intervention, deviation from intended intervention, missing data and measurement of outcomes was determined to be low. For two studies, the possibility of bias due to selection of reported results was considered to be low. 35 37 Seven studies were identified as probably having a serious risk of bias mostly due to potential confounding and the selection of reported results. 36 38-43
elements.reason: Provides an overall summary (two moderate, seven serious) and general domain-level statements, but does not present per-study domain-level and overall judgements in a table or figure. Details appear relegated to supplemental material, which is not provided here.

elements.quote: Seven studies were identified as probably having a serious risk of bias mostly due to potential confounding and the selection of reported results.
elements.reason: Offers general reasons for high risk-of-bias assessments, but does not provide justifications for each specific judgement (by study and domain).
No evidence that outcome-specific risk-of-bias judgements are displayed alongside study results; only aggregate statements about risk of bias are reported.
No extracted text shows per-study, per-outcome group-level summary statistics reported in the Results; referenced tables/supplements are not provided in the retrieved evidence.
Although methods describe extracting/calculating effect measures and CIs, no retrieved Results content presents effect estimates with precision for each study and outcome.

elements.quote: Table 1 presents the characteristics of interventions and findings for all outcomes of importance.
elements.reason: Indicates a structured tabular display of findings is provided.

elements.quote: In the case that in these studies enough data points for an outcome were presented in a readable graph or a table, the available data was re- analysed using an ITS design as described above.
elements.reason: Study-level data appear to come from the included articles (graphs/tables) rather than multiple data sources for the same study data; no indication that multiple sources were used, so the condition does not apply.

elements.quote: In the case that in these studies enough data points for an outcome were presented in a readable graph or a table, the available data was re- analysed using an ITS design as described above. In total, outcomes measured and reported in six studies (67%) were re- analysed. All outcomes reported in the included studies, along with information on whether these outcomes could be re- analysed, are presented in online supplemental material 1.
elements.reason: The authors explicitly state that some results were re-analysed (computed) and indicate where these computed results are identified.

elements.reason: No retrieved evidence reports any sensitivity analyses or their results.
No discussion was found on the robustness of the main analysis in light of sensitivity analyses.
No tables comparing original and sensitivity-analysis results, assumptions, or contributing studies were identified in the retrieved evidence.
No forest plots displaying sensitivity-analysis results were found in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: The overall rating for certainty in estimates was very low for the outcome mortality (in- hospital; 30 days). The outcomes complications, reoperations, length of stay and travel distance were rated as of low certainty of evidence.
elements.reason: Reports overall certainty levels for each of the five prespecified important outcomes (mortality, complications, reoperations, length of stay, travel distance).

elements.quote: Results on outcomes of seven out of nine studies are considered to be at serious risk of bias. The certainty of evidence is very low for mortality (in- hospital; 30 days) and low for complications, reoperations, length of stay and travel distance. The results are based on a relatively small number of studies for most outcomes... there is still a potential for publication bias.
elements.reason: Provides general reasons (serious risk of bias, small number of studies, potential publication bias) but does not explicitly link GRADE downgrading/upgrade reasons to each outcome or domain.

elements.quote: Minimum volume standards in hospitals may result in a reduction of the mean length of stay (low certainty of evidence).
elements.reason: Certainty is communicated alongside at least one reported result (length of stay). However, available evidence does not confirm that certainty is presented with all outcomes wherever results are reported.

elements.quote: The GRADE assessments are reported in the summary of findings table (table 2).
elements.reason: States inclusion of a GRADE Summary of Findings table.

elements.quote: Overall, considering the evidence for the volume- outcome relationship in hospitals, 44 45 the lack of findings in our systematic review with respect to complication and mortality rates is noteworthy. More precisely, evidence whether the introduction of minimum volume standards based on the volume- outcome relationship, leads to improved complication and mortality rates, is still lacking. ... This finding is in line with the results of a systematic review on minimum volume standards in day surgery. 20 46
elements.reason: The discussion explicitly interprets the review’s findings against prior evidence (the established volume–outcome relationship) and notes alignment with another systematic review, thereby placing results in the context of other evidence.

elements.quote: Results on outcomes of seven out of nine studies are considered to be at serious risk of bias. The certainty of evidence is very low for mortality (in- hospital; 30 days) and low for complications, reoperations, length of stay and travel distance. The results are based on a relatively small number of studies for most outcomes. ... Only three of nine (33%) included studies had a thorough study design that could be clearly identified as either a CBA ... or an ITS. ... there is still a potential for publication bias.
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly discusses limitations of the included evidence, including high risk of bias in most studies, low/very low certainty of evidence, small number of studies, limited robust study designs, and potential publication bias.

elements.quote: This is mostly due to our restriction to only include studies with a robust study design (eg, CBA or ITS studies). … Despite the efforts to include grey literature, the search for conference abstracts and contacting authors, there is still a potential for publication bias.
elements.reason: The authors explicitly discuss review-process limitations: restrictive eligibility criteria (only robust designs) and residual publication bias despite extensive searching.

elements.quote: The results are based on a relatively small number of studies for most outcomes. This is mostly due to our restriction to only include studies with a robust study design (eg, CBA or ITS studies). … Despite the efforts to include grey literature, the search for conference abstracts and contacting authors, there is still a potential for publication bias. Thus, reported outcomes should be interpreted with caution.
elements.reason: They describe the impact of the process limitations: restrictive inclusion led to a small evidence base, and potential publication bias necessitates cautious interpretation of the outcomes.

elements.quote: As expected, the distance between the patient's residence and the treating hospital statistically significantly increased during the process of centralisation through the implementation of minimum volume standards in both studies.
elements.reason: This notes a concrete practice-related impact (increased travel distance affecting service delivery and patient access), but the manuscript does not elaborate explicit practical guidance or recommendations; hence only a partial discussion of practice implications.

elements.quote: To ascertain the effectiveness of the implemented minimum volume standards, we recommend conducting evaluations of existing minimum volume standards as part of the respective implementation process.
elements.reason: Provides a clear policy implication by recommending that evaluations be embedded within the implementation of minimum volume standards.

elements.quote: However, to evaluate the effects of minimum volume standards in hospitals, study designs as recommended by EPOC should be employed. Particularly, as (C)RCTs and nRCTs cannot be conducted in the context of minimum volume standards, controlled before- after studies or interrupted time series studies with at least three data points prior and post- intervention are needed. ... Given that most studies rely on registry or administrative data, increasing the number of observation points is generally feasible and could enhance the use of ITS analyses.
elements.reason: Offers explicit recommendations for future research, specifying appropriate study designs (CBA, ITS) and methodological details (minimum data points, increasing observation points).

elements.quote: A priori, the systematic review was registered in the Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO registration number CRD42022318883) and a protocol was published.
elements.reason: Explicitly reports the review register name (PROSPERO) and the registration number (CRD42022318883).

elements.quote: A priori, the systematic review was registered in the Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO registration number CRD42022318883) and a protocol was published. 22
elements.reason: The authors provide a PROSPERO registration number and indicate a published protocol with a citation marker (22), identifying where the protocol can be accessed.

elements.quote: As an amendment to the published protocol, we also accepted policies which combined minimum volume standards with certain co- interventions, that is, training of medical staff.
elements.reason: An amendment to the protocol is described, but it is not clear whether this is the only amendment or whether all amendments are reported.
No reason is provided for the reported amendment in the retrieved evidence.
The stage of the review at which the amendment was implemented is not reported in the retrieved evidence.
